title: Marta
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Pesachim 103a we find: “Marta said in Rabbi Yehoshua’s name: ניה״ק.” He is mentioned there alongside Levi and Mar, son of Ravna. It is not known who this Marta was or who this Rabbi Yehoshua was. The better reading is that of Dikdukei Soferim there, note vav: “Marona, in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.” The word Marona became corrupted into Marta when the vav and nun joined, producing a tav. He is in fact Marin, who spoke in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name in Eruvin 19a.[^1]

notes.text: The mnemonic ניה״ק is retained without an expansion; the earlier English “this is what he meant” was unsupported. Mar’s patronymic is printed רבנא and is transliterated Ravna without identifying him with another named sage. The customary expansions of דק״ס and רי״בל are Dikdukei Soferim and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi; the specific edition has not been established here. The cited note is identified by the letter ו׳ (vav). The preference for Marona, the proposed joining of letters and the identification with Marin are Hyman’s textual argument, with its original confidence retained; they are not independently established identifications. Hyman’s Eruvin locator ends with two periods, יט..; 19a is its conventional reading, not a verified modern locus. Neither cited passage was independently checked.
